amazing game, one of my personal most anticipated releases of 2025 and something i've played for the last few months as my main MP point and click shooter. is the game being a TPS kinda wack for an extraction shooter? sure, especially if you're not used to it in the genre. is your lobby experience totally based on how nice or cruel your fellow players and ARC? absolutely. is the game balance perfect? no, not that much. 

BUT, these are not faults of Embark nor ARC Raiders. sure you will run into dirtbags, rats, extract campers and pretend friendlies but that's the whole damn point of an extraction shooter! you need to use your gut instict to survive. don't blindly trust people, don't turn your back on suspicious characters and at the end of the day if you get cornered and you can't shoot your way out, just run. there are SO many tools avaliable to deal with so many issues people ♥♥♥♥♥ about. you really wanna PVP but you hate people who team in solos? pick your fights! trying to extract in a notoriously bad place? toss some tagging nades down and check your corners. getting shot in the back? don't put away your weapon and be ready for a fight if you ask if they're friendly and don't respond.

same with arc and gun balancing, it can be quite annoying to deal with shredders (really, ♥♥♥♥ those guys) and rocketeers but stay calm and play ring around the rosie or toss a lure nade and you'll be fine. getting smacked all the time by a guy corner peeking you with a vulcano? it's fine, even with a rattler or a ferro the TTK is high enough where you can always evaluate your fights and play smart, regardless of how kitted you are. at the end of the day, you shouldn't be getting mad at the game for issues you can easily handle. you get what you put in and if you're just looking for a PURE pvp experience or a hugbox robot killing sim you're gonna be disappointed. but if you open your mind, use some common sense and enjoy Arc Raiders for what it is, a game, with all it's high highs and low lows you will fall in love with it.

i'm not even going to go into too much depth when it comes to other small details like sound design, artstyle, cosmetics, monetisation or that sort of jazz, i am by no means an expert game journalist and dunno what to write. BUT as a casual player with 20 in Charisma I've gotten so many hilarious moments, adrenaline pumping gunfights and too many embarrassing deaths to pops and I can safely say that from playing the first closed alpha it's everything I've ever wanted from a game. addictive, crazy fun, and the only complaint is that it needs more things to do but Embark feverishly works on their games so I expect great things in the future (just look at The Finals)

Edit: I found my issue. For some reason AMD has overclocking on by default and it was causing Unreal to crash and easy anti cheat flagging files and closing the game. In the BIOS I had to change AI overclock tuner to EXPO I, and AMD overclocking to disable. Played over 10 hours since and no crashing. Leaving the rest of my review incase it helps someone else on what I did to solve all the crashing issues I had.

Yah it looks weird having over 100 hours and I'm not recommending this game. I have a PC that's 2 months old and I've been fighting this game for a month dealing with Unreal and easy anti-cheat crashing the game. I've tried dozens of fix attempts looking online, wrote pages of notes of what I tried. Some fix attempts I had no idea what I was doing, like editing my registry. Here's most of what I attempted:

In adrenalin, turn off Fidelity FX super resolution 4

In BIOS, change AI overclock tuner from auto to manual and frequency to 100.

Turned off Windows "fast startup".

Disable EXPO in my BIOS, set RAM speed to 6000 (not overclocking it)

Steam > game properties > Launch options, tried -dx11.

Restore Adrenalin to default in case is messed up something.

Ran DISM to repair corrupted files.

In registry edit, I added TdrDelay and TdrDdiDelay that I saw in a video.

Reset shaders and set ray tracing to static.

Ran MemTest86 and my RAM is not the issue.

Used DDU utility to completely remove graphics drivers and reinstall.

Clear directx shader cashe.

Disable Discord/AMD overlays, un/reinstall easy anti cheat and verified game files.

Device manager, disable "AMD Radeon (TM)" driver so it'd use "Radeon RX 9070 XT".

Physically reseat my RAM in case something was loose and reapply thermal grease.

Set my frame limit to 120.

Repair Microsoft visual C++ (both x64 and x 86).

Make sure windows is up to date.

In command, fsc /scannow, DISM /online /cleanup-image /restorehealth.

Used Revo uninstaller to remove Arc then reinstall.

Deleted "discord_partner_sdk.dll" and had it download when I verified files.

At this point I formatted my HD and reinstalled windows and the minimal programs to run the game.

Rolled back CPU and video drivers. It still got me the Unreal violation crash and another type that was new to me.

With over 100 hours I got my moneys worth. I'm nearly giving up.

ARC Raiders is an excellent extraction shooter that stands out with its polished gameplay and accessible design. It delivers the tension and depth expected from the genre while remaining very approachable for new players.

As a third-person extraction shooter, ARC Raiders offers a refreshing and highly playable alternative to Escape from Tarkov. The third-person perspective improves situational awareness and makes combat feel more fluid and readable, especially for beginners who may find traditional hardcore shooters overwhelming.

The game strikes a great balance between challenge and accessibility. Core mechanics such as looting, extraction, and combat are intuitive, while still leaving plenty of room for mastery and strategic play. Progression feels rewarding without being punishing, making it easy to learn but hard to put down.

Overall, ARC Raiders is a superb extraction shooter with strong design choices, smooth gameplay, and a beginner-friendly approach. Highly recommended for both veterans of the genre and players looking for a more approachable Tarkov-style experience.

TLDR: Embarq took a potentially great game and ruined it because big man CEO wanted Fortnite money.

The game has player behavior based matchmaking. Shoot other players, It matches you with people who shoot other players. Don't shoot other players, get matched with MOSTLY others like you. But there's always a chance that someone's gonna try to kill you. It's an okay system until you refuse to turn the other cheek. You literally have to play full pacifism mode to get matched with MOSTLY non-toxic players, which means there is always a chance you will get shot at. If you dare to shoot back a player, even if they had just murdered another player, the algorithm says "Oh, you must like pvp" and throws you right back into the bucket of crabs.

You can't actually talk to other players from a distance, you have to let them get close enough to kill you to hear them, and usually the first one to get shot dies.

Players can load in with a free loadout, which is a randomized set of one common weapon, a little ammo, some healing items, grenades and utilities. It's great for players low on supplies, but terrible because people have to put nothing but time on the line, and can potentially leave with top tier loot and waste the time AND supplies of someone else. This encourages players to camp extraction points and ambush people after they've done all of the looting for them. Unless you are looking for specific items, this is the most efficient tactic to gain value in the game. You don't have to risk fighting the ARC, and you're calm and collected while your targets are shaken from running around fighting ARC and other players with a backpack full of the good stuff to lose. 

The extraction points are constructed in a way that promotes this behavior. Calling for extraction triggers a massive audio queue that alerts anyone nearby. To finalize the extraction you have to interact with a terminal for several seconds, which leaves you defenseless. If you take damage while doing this, it cancels the interaction. There are plenty of hiding spots to lie in wait as well. The game is made to promote extract camping, ambushes, and betrayals.

You can't move fast without putting your weapon away. You have to be a fish in a barrel to get around the map efficiently. Why do that when you can just spawn in with a free loadout crouch in a bush or camp extract and get the first shot on the people gathering the loot?

I've been shot at and killed during Matriarch events, where the players are trying to take down large enemies as a group and you have to bring a lot of gear to get the job done. People will shoot you for trying to loot the bots, even if you help to kill the bots. People will also do the free loadout thing here in the hopes of taking out a player that actually spent hours gathering guns and material to stock up to help kill the boss. They usually die for the attempt, but they lose nothing but time if they fail and gain top tier stuff if they succeed, so why not? You can easily lose over 100K in gear value on these chasing an item with a value of 13K that you need to craft some things.

If the game had a dedicated PvE mode, it MIGHT be great, but these rat players would probably flock there to throw lure grenades or snitch drivers at others to ruin it.

This game actually makes you into a worse person. Punishes trust. Punishes dishing out justice. Punishes peacefully gathering loot. Rewards predatory rat behavior. And again, all because a CEO played it, thought it was missing something, and then reused all the existing assets to make it into a Tarkov clone and said "Yeah, this is a good game now". It's a terrible game, made from the bones of a good one by terrible people, for other terrible people. If that sounds like your cup of tea, then please play this game instead of interacting with the real world.

It's a really good game, but I believe this was MUCH better in the first few weeks/month when people were still getting the hang of it.

Now that most people who play fully understand the mechanics, its genuinely more PvP with a bit of PvE thrown in. Within the first few weeks, you could trust most people, and there would be dialogue before any encounters (mostly).

Now it seems with streamers, everyone wants to replicate this and it's immediately shoot on site anything that moves. No teaming up, no battling the enemy together. Its pretty much PvP in the hope that you win and return with loot. 

The other annoying thing (Which shouldn't be a thing), is joining a game in progress. I joined with my own loadout, took 5 steps forward and there was a camper waiting on my spawn. How the hell is it fair that, the loot which I have worked for, is rewarded to somebody sat on a spawn?

Ingredients
2 x 400g beef fillets
Olive oil, for frying
500g mixture of wild mushrooms, cleaned
1 thyme sprig, leaves only
500g puff pastry
8 slices of Parma ham
2 egg yolks, beaten with 1 tbsp water and a pinch of salt
Sea salt and freshly ground black pepper
For the red wine sauce

2 tbsp olive oil
200g beef trimmings (ask the butcher to reserve these when trimming the fillet)
4 large shallots, peeled and sliced
12 black peppercorns
1 bay leaf
1 thyme sprig
Splash of red wine vinegar
1 x 750ml bottle red wine
750ml beef stock
 
Method
Serves 4

Wrap each piece of beef tightly in a triple layer of cling film to set its shape, then chill overnight.

Remove the cling film, then quickly sear the beef fillets in a hot pan with a little olive oil for 30-60 seconds until browned all over and rare in the middle. Remove from the pan and leave to cool.

Finely chop the mushrooms and fry in a hot pan with a little olive oil, the thyme leaves and some seasoning. When the mushrooms begin to release their juices, continue to cook over a high heat for about 10 minutes until all the excess moisture has evaporated and you are left with a mushroom paste (known as a duxelle). Remove the duxelle from the pan and leave to cool.

Cut the pastry in half, place on a lightly floured surface and roll each piece into a rectangle large enough to envelop one of the beef fillets. Chill in the refrigerator.

Lay a large sheet of cling film on a work surface and place 4 slices of Parma ham in the middle, overlapping them slightly, to create a square. Spread half the duxelle evenly over the ham.

Season the beef fillets, then place them on top of the mushroom-covered ham. Using the cling film, roll the Parma ham over the beef, then roll and tie the cling film to get a nice, evenly thick log. Repeat this step with the other beef fillet, then chill for at least 30 minutes.

Brush the pastry with the egg wash. Remove the cling film from the beef, then wrap the pastry around each ham-wrapped fillet. Trim the pastry and brush all over with the egg wash. Cover with cling film and chill for at least 30 minutes.

Meanwhile, make the red wine sauce. Heat the oil in a large pan, then fry the beef trimmings for a few minutes until browned on all sides. Stir in the shallots with the peppercorns, bay and thyme and continue to cook for about 5 minutes, stirring frequently, until the shallots turn golden brown.

Pour in the vinegar and let it bubble for a few minutes until almost dry. Now add the wine and boil until almost completely reduced. Add the stock and bring to the boil again. Lower the heat and simmer gently for 1 hour, removing any scum from the surface of the sauce, until you have the desired consistency. Strain the liquid through a fine sieve lined with muslin. Check for seasoning and set aside.

When you are ready to cook the beef wellingtons, score the pastry lightly and brush with the egg wash again, then bake at 200°C/Gas 6 for 15-20 minutes until the pastry is golden brown and cooked. Rest for 10 minutes before carving.

Meanwhile, reheat the sauce. Serve the beef wellingtons sliced, with the sauce as an accompaniment.

I absolutely recommend if you don't mind the occasional loss. Dying in this game is such a big deal, so if you can shrug it off the game is perfect. The sound design is possibly the best in the industry right now, the world feels alive, the guns feel great to shoot, the aesthetic is like a fallout-esque 70's sci-fi. 

The only downside I'll give this game is that the PVE enemies are so interesting and unique to fight that having a lack of a PVE-Only mode feels like a crime. You will meet enemy players, friendly players, and friendlies that will stab you in the back, and a lot of people get tired of the mind-crisping fear of death by pvp.
